stimuli.description: Two distinct architectural contexts (modern interior classroom and meeting room, 7m x 8m x 3m) each featuring five different artificial lighting conditions (Warm-Dark, Cold-Dark, Neutral-Moderate, Warm-Bright, Cold-Bright) within a virtual environment. Lighting conditions varied in luminous flux (600 lm to 4200 lm) and Correlated Color Temperature (2000 K to 7200 K).

limitations: Measurements utilized in the study have yet to be validated against real-world measurement methods.
Findings should be interpreted with caution and are possibly limited to the sampled sub-population (convenience sampling of university students and young adults).
The proportion of participants wearing eyeglasses could be different from the general population and may lead to difference effects of lighting condition on task performance.
Constraint in the geographical location during the data collection.
Experiment performed using relatively low-difficulty tasks.
VR displays limitations in luminance range, impacting effectiveness in extremely high or low illuminance situations.
VR displays cannot reproduce the same high intensities as real-world light sources, hindering accurate simulation of blinding effects and glare.
VR falls short in depicting low-light settings accurately, as current displays cannot reproduce scotopic vision range conditions.
